name: DecalMeshBuilder
src_typeComment: The actual "mesh-projected decal" technique: clips each candidate source triangle against a unit projection BOX (Sutherland-Hodgman, one pass per box face) rather than rendering a flat quad on top of the surface or splatting into a render texture — the decal is built FROM the receiving geometry's own triangles, so it follows curved/uneven surfaces exactly rather than floating or clipping through them. Pure and stateless (candidate triangles passed in, a Mesh handed back) so the clipping math is testable with synthetic triangles, no scene/GameObjects required.

src_members.name: Build
src_members.comment: candidateTriangles: each entry is one source triangle as (a, b, c, normal), all in WORLD space. worldToDecal / decalToWorld: the projection box's own transform, sized so decal-local space IS the [-0.5, 0.5] unit cube (i.e. built from Matrix4x4.TRS(position, rotation, boxSize)). maxSurfaceAngleDegrees: a triangle whose normal points more than this many degrees away from straight down the box's local -Y axis (the projection direction) is skipped entirely — keeps a floor decal from wrapping onto a nearby wall. surfaceOffset: world-space push along each vertex's own normal, away from the surface, to avoid z-fighting with the geometry the decal sits on.
